claims: NHL playoff overtime consists of 20-minute periods.
NHL playoff overtime periods are sudden-death.
NHL playoff overtime is played until a team scores.
There are no shootouts in NHL playoff overtime.
If the score remains tied, additional 20-minute periods are played after a 15-minute intermission.
The teams change ends for each overtime period.
Playoff overtime format is 5-on-5 (5 skaters + 1 goalie).
Playoff overtime periods are full 20-minute periods, not 5-minute periods.
The first team to score wins immediately in sudden death.
A 15-minute intermission follows the end of regulation (third period), with ice resurfacing.
If no team scores in the first overtime, a second 20-minute period is played, and so on, until a winner is determined.
During long, multi-overtime games, only a dry scrape (shoveling loose ice) is performed at the first stoppage after the period is half-finished, rather than a full ice resurfacing.
These rules apply to all games in the Stanley Cup Playoffs.
